articles.title: Steven Spielberg’s Ready Player One improves immensely on the book
articles.summary: Ernest Cline’s fast-moving, bestselling novel was a treasure trove for pop-culture junkies. But the endless references to video games and movies work better on the screen, where most of them originated in the first place.
articles.body: Fans tend to either love or hate Ernest Cline’s bestselling 2011 novel Ready Player One. There are legitimate reasons for both reactions. On the love side: it’s a light, airy pop confection, crammed with familiar cultural references, which Cline recontextualizes in surprising ways. On the hate side: the prose can be extremely clumsy, as it is in this paragraph where teenage protagonist Wade Watts describes the virtual car he constructed for himself in the vast online world where he spends most of his waking hours: > The DeLorean came outfitted with a (nonfunctioning) flux capacitor, but I’d made several additions to its equipment and appearance. First, I’d installed an artificially intelligent onboard computer named KITT (purchased in an online auction) into the dashboard, along with a matching red Knight Rider scanner just above the DeLorean’s grill. Then I’d outfitted the car with an oscillation overthruster, a device that allowed it to travel through solid matter. Finally, to complete my ‘80s super-vehicle theme, I’d slapped a Ghostbusters logo on each of the DeLorean’s gull-wing doors, then added personalized plates that read ECTO-88. That’s a lot of awkward verbiage to say two pretty basic things: people in virtual reality can express their personal tastes through their avatars in hyper-specific ways, and Cline is so obsessed with the culture of the 1980s — the geek-fodder of his youth — that he thinks it’s compelling even in the form of a shopping list. The book is a fast-paced adventure, but this kind of unwieldy lump of mix-and-match nostalgia acts as a roadblock. There’s no attempt to consider why Wade finds these specific objects appealing, out of the billion options available to him. The book assumes up front that readers find everything in this list as unbearably cool as Cline does, and that just running down an exhaustive list of Wade’s favorite things is enough to make him appealing, relatable, and enviable. Steven Spielberg’s new film adaptation of Ready Player One prominently features that same car, but in a context that improves it immensely. Spielberg doesn’t have Wade talk audiences through it, and he doesn’t spell out the references. He just slaps the car down in the middle of a tremendous early action scene, where it’s prominent, distinctive, and memorable. Fans who want the full nostalgia trip, who want to wring every Easter egg out of the experience, will eventually be able to pause the movie and frame-by-frame through it, looking for the flux capacitor on the dashboard, checking the plates, and scanning for extra bonus material. But in the middle of the action, even to people who’ve never seen the Back to the Future movies and aren’t vibing on the connection, the car doesn’t need explaining. It’s just a sleek piece of visual energy, one breathless element among dozens of others. It’s not a citation or a list. It’s an effortless, integrated piece of the action. [Media: That dynamic stretches throughout Ready Player One, scripted by Cline and X-Men: The Last Stand writer Zak Penn, and directed by Spielberg as a whiplash-fast tear through a world-spanning, all-encompassing video game. The story, which mostly takes place in the virtual-reality world called The OASIS, rarely slows down enough to explain the references, or geek out over them the way the book does. It’s still a visual festival of ‘80s culture that sometimes hinges significant jokes on the assumption that the audience knows the filmography of Robert Zemeckis, or will chortle over a reference to Monty Python and the Holy Grail. But the film improves significantly on the book by prioritizing the story over the signifiers. The hardcore pop-culture crowd that is this movie’s ultimate intended audience will have plenty to pore over and pick apart in this film. But the story moves briskly enough, and with enough giant-sized, screen-friendly excitement, that it doesn’t feel like it’s aimed solely and specifically at them. Some of that speed comes at the expense of artistry. Ready Player One opens by laboriously climbing a mountain of voiceover, explaining the setting: the year is 2045, and the world is terrible. Most people live in depressing poverty, and spend as much time as possible jacked into the fantasy world of the OASIS. There, they can be and do anything they want, or at least anything they can afford to buy with coins won in the universe’s eternally running video game arenas. The OASIS was created by reclusive genius James Halliday (Bridge of Spies’ Mark Rylance), who packed it with his own favorite culture. When he died, he created a three-part quest within the world, linked to his favorite films and games, but also tied to his own past regrets and frustrations. Whoever finds the three keys he’s hidden within the game world, and the ultimate Easter egg they unlock, will get full control of OASIS and Halliday’s vast fortune. The quest has created a subclass of “egg-hunters,” or “Gunters” — quest-obsessives whose full-time occupation is hunting down the keys. It’s also created an evil dystopian megacorp, run by former Halliday intern Nolan Sorrento (Ben Mendelsohn, of Rogue One and Starred Up), and devoted to gaining control of the OASIS to commercialize it. Wade (X-Men: Apocalypse’s Tye Sheridan) and his fellow Gunters — particularly too-cool-for-school solo hunter Art3mis (Olivia Cooke, also currently starring in the chilling Thoroughbreds) and Wade’s big mechanical buddy Aech (Master of None’s Lena Waithe) — all want the keys and the egg for their own personal reasons, though those are barely articulated. Cline’s book assumes everyone will know a DeLorean is cool; Spielberg’s film assumes the same thing about a teenage protagonist who loves playing video games. Wade (or Parzival, as he’s known in the OASIS) eventually develops an ethos, but for the most part, he’s like every other video gamer who’s ever sat down on a couch and hit “start” on the controller. He may appreciate the gameplay or the storyline or the people he meets online, but ultimately, he just wants that elusive win. He’s more a customized audience avatar than a real character, but that’s fitting for a world that’s so spottily drawn, at least outside of the virtual paradise where people prefer to spent their time. [Image: The film version of Ready Player One has some major advantages over the book. The exposition is just as bald, but once it’s done, Spielberg can focus on the endless dynamism of a world where anything is possible. As Wade and others follow their quest through races, battles, and puzzles, they encounter a dizzying blur of visual references that act as “Hey, remember this?” in-jokes with the audience, including some major ones that weren’t in the book. But the filmmakers also delve into Halliday’s past and his wounded psyche, in a way that gradually becomes a little touching and tragic. (A conversation with Halliday’s online avatar closely recalls a similar scene with Professor Falken in WarGames, and carries the same sense of melancholy.) The film also goes further than the book in laying out why Halliday’s retreat into a fantasy world wasn’t necessarily good for anyone — especially not for Halliday himself. No matter how validating the onscreen gags are, they’re still a reminder of a man who found more emotional resonance in Jurassic Park’s T-Rex than in a connection with a living human being. The film inevitably has its cake and eats it too when it comes to addressing wish-fulfillment fantasy and delirious nostalgia: the story can only push so far in sorrowing over Halliday’s surrender and retreat from the world, while still turning every rambunctious game setpiece into a celebration of Cline’s favorite culture. Ready Player One is so heavily inspired by and inflected with the broad, black-and-white morality of ‘80s geek culture that any attempt to find the gray areas feels slightly daring, even as it feels slightly out of place. Given that Sorrento is a buttoned-down, stony-faced idea-thief of an evil overlord, straight out of Tron, there’s not a lot of room for narrative nuance in this story. But at least Cline and Penn make the effort, acknowledging some of the biggest complaints leveled at Cline’s book, and trying to take the story a little deeper. The film version does carry over some of the book’s most notable flaws, especially a suspicious reliance on narrative convenience and coincidence. The characters are thinly drawn, and most of them are little more than cool avatars and signature moves. There’s no sense that anyone involved with the story really cares about the details of the real world in this crapsack future, given how little the real-world scenes hold together. And the film takes a particularly feather-light approach to what should be significant emotions, especially when a death that should devastate Wade is shrugged off within seconds, then brought back out for a cheap, unearned moment much later. Spielberg’s signature sentiment is operating in full force, as he builds up one highly symbolic confrontation solely for the feelings of triumph and justice it creates, and then has it come to exactly nothing. And in places, the story jumps forward so quickly that it feels like necessary connective scenes are simply missing. [Image: Unequivocally, the film’s biggest problem is the half-assed love story between Wade and Art3mis, which operates on approximately 75 percent wish-fulfillment and 25 percent apathetic inevitability. When they first encounter each other, Wade is starstruck: he knows Art3mis from her online cool-girl rep, and watching her in action, he sees her as an über-badass with leet skillz and an appealingly punk devil-may-care attitude. It’s a short, shocking jump from there to him telling her he loves her. What follows should be important and telling — she reminds him that they don’t know each other, that he’s seeing an online avatar and a mental picture he’s largely invented. (And, of course, he thinks they’re perfect for each other because she gets his references.) But the film never follows through on that mature and useful point. The insta-relationship that develops between them is as inauthentic and insulting as the central romance in Edgar Wright’s Scott Pilgrim Vs. The World, without any of the sense of irony or intentionality. It’s bad enough to follow the “hero wins the girl as a prize” model without examining it at all. It’s worse still to have the characters examine it, find the flaws, then instantly forget about them. This isn’t a movie with a long memory (except when it’s reaching back 40 years for visual gags), but it’s infuriating to see it try to examine its own tropes responsibly, then take no steps whatsoever to address the issues it raises. And yet, when Wade is in his kitted-out DeLorean, tearing along a preposterously difficult game racetrack, menaced by King Kong and dodging flying debris as his fellow racers crash and burn, very little of that matters. The sheer dynamism and energy of the movie are compelling, even when the character drama isn’t. The action scenes are deliberately overclocked and overwhelming, turning Wade’s quest into a thrilling blur of fast-paced decisions and the endorphin-rush highs of a good gaming experience. More importantly, the film is overtly funny in ways that constantly remind the audience that there are people behind the game avatars, and specifically people who are sometimes young, self-absorbed, immature, and caught up in their own created self-images of badassery. The human frailties behind the game avatars is a reliable well of humor for Ready Player One, and the script takes full, hilarious advantage. And while the film’s real world gets left behind in the rush, the attention to detail during the OASIS scenes is absolutely astounding — not just the details Cline salivated over on the page, like that Knight Rider scanner in the grill of Wade’s car, but the subtle nuances, like the way Wade’s avatar constantly seems to be standing in a flattering breeze that ruffles his hair in the most winsome way possible, or the way Art3mis’ too-big anime eyes catch the light. The uncanny-valley effect is strong in these game avatars, but Spielberg uses it to his advantage, reminding his audience at every moment that what they’re seeing is mostly a fantasy, created by people who see image as almost everything. It’s a slick, sleek, surface fantasy, for sure. But for people who share Cline’s worldview, or identify with gamer culture in general, it’s an immense hit of validation and acknowledgement, delivered with joyful abandon and unmissable enthusiasm. All those feelings of love and obsession came through clearly on the page. But on the screen, they’re bigger and better, because they’re so much more intense, and so much closer to the memorable images that turned Cline into an obsessive in the first place. This review was initially published after Ready Player One’s premiere at the 2018 SXSW festival in Austin, Texas. The film arrives in theaters on March 29th, 2018.

articles.title: Hawkeye’s first season is a welcome holiday surprise
articles.summary: Season 1 of Hawkeye on Disney Plus is a six-episode romp that manages to be a fun Christmas adventure while also tying into the greater Marvel Cinematic Universe in multiple ways.
articles.body: Hawkeye is the most unassuming of the Marvel shows on Disney Plus so far. It doesn’t have the immediate hook of Loki’s time-bending story or WandaVision’s surreal take on sitcoms. It also stars arguably the most forgettable of all the Avengers, one who is getting a big spotlight while other, more notable characters get movies that come years too late. And yet… there’s something about its blend of detective story, MCU action, and charming Christmas vibe that just works. Across its six episodes, Hawkeye manages to balance being a superhero show that doesn’t take itself too seriously with all of the complex storytelling elements that come with being part of the Marvel universe. The fact that it pulls it all off so well is something of a Christmas miracle. This review contains some light spoilers for the first season of Hawkeye. Despite the name, Hawkeye isn’t a show just about Jeremy Renner’s take on the bow-wielding hero Clint Barton. He’s a big part of it, sure, but the story is just as much about his wannabe protégé Kate Bishop (Hailee Steinfeld). The two are forced together after Kate dons the costume of a vigilante known as the Ronin — formerly worn by Clint — putting her in the crosshairs of some very dangerous people. Clint just wants to be left alone to spend time with his family over the holidays, while Kate, who grew up idolizing Hawkeye, couldn’t be more thrilled about being forced together. The show’s main strength is how the two play off each other. Kate is exceedingly charming, a playful mess who is constantly in over her head, and yet usually able to talk her way out of it. Clint is the opposite: sullen, pessimistic, but prepared like Batman. The story is structured a bit like a detective story, at least at first, with the two investigating a bunch of shady people connected to the Ronin. Oh, and also, it’s Christmas in New York. This all lends the show a gritty-yet-playful vibe that suits it well, where gunfights are interrupted by quips about USB standards. It doesn’t take too long before the show intersects with the rest of the MCU — and it does so from a few different directions. [Image: One of the main connections was teased at the end of Black Widow: Yelena (Florence Pugh) vows to avenge her sister’s death by killing Clint. When she does show up to do just that, she’s equal parts menacing and hilarious (much like in Black Widow), a trained-from-birth killer who is also trying to do some normal human stuff now that she’s (sort of) free. Pugh and Steinfeld have incredible chemistry — Steinfeld seems to have great chemistry with just about everyone — and it’s a lot of fun to watch them talk life and death over a pot of macaroni and cheese, discussing everything from a planned killing to Rudolph, the “super-powered reindeer.” Later on, the two can’t stop complimenting each other in the midst of a brutal fistfight, with Kate telling Yelena, “Stop making me like you.” While Marvel fans knew that one was coming, the other big connection is much more unexpected. The big bad of season 1 is the criminal overlord Kingpin, and in this case, he’s played by Vincent D’Onofrio, who also had the role on Netflix’s Daredevil. It’s unexpected primarily because, since the launch of Disney Plus and the new wave of MCU streaming series that came with it, the fate of the Netflix shows and characters has been a source of much debate. All I’m saying is, next time an MCU character needs some help with an investigation, Jessica Jones is right there. These kinds of crossovers are common for Marvel, and for the most part, they don’t feel too obtrusive here. (Nothing is as bad as, say, Jonathan Majors’ monologue at the end of Loki.) The reveals hit a little harder if you know what’s already happened — I would recommend at least watching Black Widow first — but otherwise, the background knowledge isn’t strictly necessary to understand that Kingpin is a mob mastermind, and Yelena is a charming assassin. Hawkeye balances things nicely, making it work fairly well both for the die-hards and those coming in fresh. [Image: There are maybe a few too many threads happening concurrently, though, particularly towards the end. There’s an important villain reveal; the inevitable showdown between Clint and Yelena; the debut of some much-teased superhero costumes; a pivotal moment for Echo (Alaqua Cox), a future hero who starts out as a criminal; Kate’s seeming ascendance to Hawkeye-level hero; and of course, a tease for what comes next, which in this case appears to involve Clint’s wife, Laura Barton (Linda Cardellini). (Surprisingly, Hawkeye doesn’t have the traditional MCU big reveal after the credits; instead, viewers get to watch a full-song performance from the goofy Avengers musical from the first episode.) There’s a lot going on — at one point in the finale, there are three pivotal fights happening concurrently — and the last episode rushes through some of them without giving much time for the heavy moments to land. This kind of balancing act is, of course, key to the whole Marvel machine, where every story is just one cog in a much bigger machine. Hawkeye pulls it off as well as any of its contemporaries. It works as a standalone story, a fun romp through Christmas in New York, while also weaving in multiple threads from various other Marvel stories and setting up at least two more. All that in just six episodes — and while rehabilitating Clint Barton into a hero you finally care about.

articles.title: Marvel unveils the gigantic cast for Avengers: Doomsday
articles.summary: Marvel has shared some of the casting news for Avengers: Doomsday, which hits theaters in May 2026.
articles.body: After an hours-long tease, Marvel has confirmed much of the cast for the next Avengers movie — and it pulls together a huge list of stars from films ranging from past Avengers and X-Men flicks to Black Panther: Wakanda Forever and the upcoming Fantastic Four: First Steps. Today’s announcements include: * Chris Hemsworth (Thor) * Vanessa Kirby (Invisible Woman) * Anthony Mackie (Captain America) * Sebastian Stan (Bucky Barnes) * Letitia Wright (Black Panther) * Paul Rudd (Ant-Man) * Wyatt Russell (John Walker) * Tenoch Huerta Mejía (Namor) * Ebon Moss-Bachrach (The Thing) * Simu Liu (Shang-Chi) * Florence Pugh (Yelena Belova) * Kelsey Grammer (Beast) * Lewis Pullman (Sentry) * Danny Ramirez (Falcon) * Joseph Quinn (Human Torch) * David Harbour (Red Guardian) * Winston Duke (M’Baku) * Hannah John-Kamen (Ghost) * Tom Hiddleston (Loki) * Patrick Stewart (Charles Xavier) * Ian McKellen (Magneto) * Alan Cumming (Nightcrawler) * Rebecca Romijn (Mystique) * James Marsden (Cyclops) * Channing Tatum (Gambit) * Pedro Pascal (Mister Fantastic) Avengers: Doomsday and Secret Wars are two of the tentpoles of Marvel’s upcoming phase 6 of the Marvel Cinematic Universe. They’ll see the return of both the Russo brothers as directors and Robert Downey Jr., who’ll be swapping the Iron Man mask for Doctor Doom. Marvel reportedly spent big to get the band back together. Phase 6 will actually kick off this year with Fantastic Four, which is slated to hit theaters on July 25th, just after the premiere of Thunderbolts on May 2nd. Doomsday, meanwhile, is due out on May 1st, 2026.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday’s first trailer puts everyone on high alert
articles.summary: Avengers: Doomsday — in theaters December 18th — pits the heroes against one another in its first trailer.
articles.body: After months of teasing us with reminders about how large Avengers: Doomsday’s cast is going to be, Marvel has finally released a proper trailer for the film. Though Robert. Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom definitely appears to be causing a lot of the chaos in Doomsday’s first trailer, the movie seems like it’s going to feature more than a few moments where different teams of heroes fight one another. Thor (Chris Hemsworth) seems to be the only person who understands that the X-Men, the Fantastic Four, and the (New) Avengers need to be more focused on dealing with their new Latverian enemy. And while Thor might not be able to rally the troops on his own, Steve Rogers’ (Chris Evans) presence will probably bring them all together. The trailer makes Doomsday seem like it’s going to be another humongous spectacle that puts a lot of emphasis on our nostalgia for Marvel’s old X-Men movies. Marvel probably has a few more Doomsday details we won’t hear about until the studio comes to San Diego Comic-Con later this week, which should get people even more hyped to see the film before it hits theaters on December 18th — the same day that Dune: Part Three hits theaters.

articles.title: Andrew Rannells Was Told to ‘Stay Away’ From Kevin Spacey After Meeting Backstage at ‘The Book of Mormon’; He Then Sent a ‘Handwritten Letter’ ‘Asking Me on a Date’
articles.summary: Andrew Rannells recently revealed that Kevin Spacey asked him out while the “Girls” actor was starring in “The Book of Mormon” on Broadway. “I’ve never told...
articles.body:
Andrew Rannells recently revealed that Kevin Spacey asked him out while the "Girls" actor was starring in "The Book of Mormon" on Broadway.

"I've never told this story before. He asked me on a date once," Rannells said while guesting on "The Downside" podcast hosted by Gianmarco Soresi. "He sent me a letter to 'The Book of Mormon.' Handwritten." The actors went on to explain that the Oscar winner came to see the musical and "came backstage" to meet him after the show.

"There were always a lot of really fun people there, but sometimes they would bring them up into our dressing rooms, but with no notice," he said. "So after the show, we're getting changed. There's a knock on my door. It was Goldie Hawn, Kevin Spacey, and Joel Schumacher. They were not together, but they all walked up together. So then we were all crammed in my dressing room."

Rannells continued: "Kevin Spacey was sort of rubbing my neck as we were standing there… Joel Schumacher, who was very close to me, he said, 'Stay away from that man.'" That prompted Spacey to respond, "Hey! C'mon, c'mon," he recalled. "And then like a week later, I got a handwritten letter from him asking me on a date." Rannells concluded by noting he "never responded" to the note.

Rannells originated the role of Elder Price in the long-running musical, performing from the show's opening in 2011 through June 2012. The part earned him a Tony nomination for best leading actor in a musical.

Spacey's sexual assault allegations came years later in 2017, when fellow Broadway actor Anthony Rapp said that the actor assaulted him in his New York apartment while Rapp was a teenager. Rapp later filed a $40 million civil lawsuit for sexual assault and battery in 2022, but a New York jury found Spacey not liable on all counts. Earlier this year, Spacey reached a settlement with three men who sued him over sexual assault claims, avoiding a civil trial in London that was set for October.

articles.title: Festival de Artes Híbridas de Sorocaba ocupa o Parque da Biquinha | G1
articles.standfirst: O Festival de Artes Híbridas começa neste sábado (28), com entrada gratuita e livre para todos os públicos.
articles.summary: Com entrada gratuita, o Festival de Artes Híbridas de Sorocaba reúne performances de Uýra Sodoma, cinema e artes visuais no Parque da Biquinha neste fim de semana.
articles.body:
Uýra Sodoma, artista convidada para o 4º Festival de Artes Híbridas de Sorocaba — Foto: Matheus Belém / Divulgação

No próximo final de semana, entre os dias 28 e 29 de novembro, o Festival de Artes Híbridas deve ocupar o Parque da Biquinha em Sorocaba (SP). O evento conta com mais de 20 obras contemporâneas e tem como objetivo proporcionar ao público uma experiência imersivas e individual com a arte.

Além da presença de artistas de diferentes estados do país, a programação deste ano dará continuidade a uma iniciativa de oferecer à comunidade local uma oportunidade de residência artística oferecendo condições para que artistas da região aprofundem suas pesquisas e desenvolvam novas obras no campo das artes performativas.

Sem um palco único ou percurso predefinido, o Festival convida o público a explorar livremente os espaços do parque, descobrindo as obras ao longo de seus próprios caminhos. Essa proposta, de acordo com Robson Catalunha, diretor e idealizador do Festival, é o que guia o diferencial do Festival.

“Ao ocupar o Parque da Biquinha, se propõe uma experiência imersiva que borra as fronteiras entre arte, natureza e cultura ”, afirma Robson.

Uýra Sodoma é uma artista indígena, performer e ativista ambiental que irá comandar a abertura do Festival no sábado (28), às 15h. Uýra também é bióloga e mestra em Ecologia, e por isso uniu em sua pesquisa artística propostas que aproximam corpo, natureza e território.

Para o Festival, a artista preparou a performance inédita "Asfalto Rasgado", que propõe um percurso do Sesc Sorocaba ao Parque da Biquinha, transformando o deslocamento pela cidade em experiência artística. Sua proposta aproxima corpo, natureza e território por meio de figuras híbridas com elementos orgânicos e vegetais.

Uýra Sodoma preparou performance inédita para Festival de Artes Híbridas — Foto: Matheus Belém / Divulgação

Outro destaque é a proposta teatral do grupo Teatro Kunyn. Neste trabalho, os artistas oferecem ao público uma espécie de "caminhada poética" por diferentes trajetos entre o Sesc Sorocaba e o Parque da Biquinha, sendo acompanhados por uma dramaturgia sonora e por ações cênicas.

Nesta edição também há a novidade de uma parceria com o Festival Mix Brasil, que traz para o Festival uma oportunidade de sessão de cinema. Três curtas-metragens foram selecionados com a temática de encontro entre cinema, inteligência artificial e diversidade.

Por fim, a programação desta edição foi definida a partir de um edital de chamamento público, que selecionou propostas nos campos das artes visuais, da performance e da dança, reunindo artistas de diferentes regiões do país. Ao todo, participam representantes de quatro estados do Sudeste e Sul brasileiro:

Performance cênica de "Como os corpos podem substituir as ideias" pela cidade — Foto: Divulgação

O Festival de Artes Híbridas acontece nos dias 28 e 29 de novembro (sábado e domingo), a partir das 15h. O Parque da Biquinha fica na Avenida Comendador Pereira Inácio, 1.112 – Jardim Emília .

A programação gratuita e livre para todos os públicos. Para mais informações, acesse as redes sociais do evento.

articles.title: 'Mineirinho' Alexandre Pires canta o samba de São Paulo em 'Sampagode', show que será gravado em janeiro com  Luiz Carlos e mais 13 convidados | G1
articles.body:
Luiz Carlos (à esquerda) é um dos 14 convidados de Alexandre Pires na gravação do álbum audiovisual 'Sampagode' — Foto: Reprodução / Vídeo Instagram Alexandre Pires

♬ Alexandre Pires nasceu em Uberlândia (MG), mas o mineirinho – epíteto cunhado em 1997 por conta da gravação da música homônima pelo Só pra Contrariar, grupo que revelou o cantor – sabe que o QG do pagode dos anos 1990 sempre esteve situado na cidade de São Paulo (SP).

É esse samba de São Paulo que Alexandre Pires exalta e revive no inédito show “Sampagode”, programado para estrear em 27 de janeiro no Espaço Unimed, em São Paulo (SP).

Por ocasião da estreia, Pires já fará o registro do show para gerar álbum audiovisual previsto para ser lançado em 2027. A gravação ao vivo de “Sampagode” será feita com produção musical de Wilson Prateado.

Ao longo das estimadas três horas de show, o cantor seguirá roteiro que transitará por todos os sucessos do pagode paulistano com participações de nada menos do que 14 convidados.

O time de convidados da gravação do show “Sampagode” inclui a cantora Eliana de Lima e os cantores Luiz Carlos – revelado como vocalista do grupo Raça Negra – e Royce do Cavaco.

articles.body:
Palácio da Música em Teresina — Foto: Ascom / FMC

O XXVI Festival de Bandas será realizado entre quinta (25) e sexta-feira (27), no Palácio da Música, em Teresina . Com entrada gratuita, o evento vai reunir 17 atrações piauienses e contará com apresentações musicais e oficinas abertas ao público.

As atividades começam sempre às 18h. Entre as atrações confirmadas estão a Banda Maestro Elton Oliveira, Banda Iêda Cadah, Banda Luiz Gonzaga, Banda Tom Jobim e a Orquestra Jovem de União.

articles.title: Britney Spears Says She Is ‘Very Sorry’ to Her ‘Beautiful Family’ for ‘Bringing Up Past Issues’ in a Now-Deleted Post
articles.summary: In a lengthy Instagram caption, Spears apologized multiple times, writing that she misses her family “like crazy”
articles.body:
Britney Spears apologized multiple times in a now-deleted Instagram post to her family for resurfacing "past issues" and not discussing them "face to face" with them

The post comes after years of Britney speaking candidly about her conflicting feelings toward family members, including dad Jamie, mom Lynne and sister Jamie Lynn

The photo used for the post was an AI-generated image of two cats having tea time in London while wearing pink and beige cardigans and matching tiny purses

Britney Spears is sharing her feelings about her estranged family.

In a now-deleted Instagram post shared on Saturday, Nov. 21, the 44-year-old pop star apologized to unnamed relatives for resurfacing "past issues," explaining that she hasn't spoken to some estranged family members "face to face" about the unspecified topics.

"I'm so blessed to have such a beautiful family," she began the post's caption. "I'm so very sorry for bringing up past issues, but I think I did because I realized I needed to protect my heart…it's the way I love and when I love you, I REALLY love you."

The mother of two continued, "My stubbornness is childish and embarrassing. Thoughts on the past, I'm obviously human and there actually might be something to those things I said [psychology] wise."

"Either way I'm sorry to my family bringing up those memories, but I've never actually spoke to them face to face on it…it's frankly bc I just miss them like crazy!!! And I'm very sorry!!!" she concluded the caption.

The photo used for the post was an AI-generated image of two cats having tea time in London while wearing pink and beige cardigans and matching tiny purses, with Big Ben standing tall outside the window in the background.

The post comes after years of Britney speaking candidly about her conflicting feelings toward family members, including her dad Jamie Spears, 74, mom Lynne Spears, 71, and sister Jamie Lynn Spears , 35.

The "Everytime" singer opened up about the family's complicated relationship in her 2023 memoir, The Woman in Me , in which she wrote that her "heart goes out" to Jamie Lynn for growing up in her shadow and for being a fellow child of divorce.

The Grammy winner has repeatedly spoken about the court-ordered conservatorship overseen by her father and a lawyer.

The conservatorship began in 2008, and in June 2021, Britney spoke for the first time about it to challenge it in court. "I've lied and told the whole world I'm okay and I'm happy," she said at the time, adding, "I'm not happy. I can't sleep. I'm depressed. I cry every day."

Jamie was removed from his role as Britney's estate conservator in September 2021 after the singer's lawyer asked the court to suspend him, and the entire conservatorship was eventually terminated that November.

articles.body: The Global Peace Honours 2026 was hosted at Mumbai's Gateway of India on Saturday, November 21, just days before the 18th anniversary of the 26/11 terror attacks. Film stars, political leaders and business names gathered to pay tribute to terror victims and the people who stood up against violence.Star-studded guest list at Gateway of IndiaThe ceremony was put together by the Divyaj Foundation and started by Amruta Fadnavis. Shah Rukh Khan, Ranveer Singh, Vivek Ranadive, Boman Irani and more attended, along with Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and his deputy, Eknath Shinde. Sadhguru was also part of the gathering.Clips from the evening are spreading fast on social media, showing guests chatting and taking part in different parts of the programme. Ranveer's stage act and Shah Rukh's conversation with a 26/11 survivor were among the most talked about moments.Ranveer Singh performs 'Dhurandhar', the title track, with changed lyricsRanveer Singh climbed on stage and danced to the title song of his film 'Dhurandhar', bringing his usual high energy to the waterfront venue. What really got noticed, though, was the modified rap by Hanumankind. The original version goes, "They call me a bad man; that's a f***ing good thing." At the event, the abusive word was dropped, and the line became, "They call me a bad man; that's a good, good thing." The song has vocals by Hanumankind, Jasmine Sandlas, Sudhir Yaduvanshi and Shashwat Sachdev, among others. Hanumankind, Jasmine Sandlas and Babu Singh Maan wrote the words, while Shashwat Sachdev and Charanjit Ahuja composed the music.Shah Rukh Khan recreates a popular film lineShah Rukh Khan also stepped up on stage and, in a playful moment, mouthed his well-known dialogue from 'Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge': "Bade bade deshon mein aisi chhoti chhoti baatein hoti rehti hain, senorita."Remembering the 26/11 Mumbai attacksThe event took place ahead of the attacks' 18th anniversary. On November 26, 2008, 10 terrorists from the Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba launched coordinated assaults across the city. They targeted the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, Oberoi-Trident, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Leopold Cafe and Nariman House.The siege dragged on until November 29, leaving 166 people dead and 238 injured. articles.body: Rashmika Mandanna has opened up about the wave of online negativity that followed her and husband Vijay Deverakonda's appearance on 'Koffee with Karan' Season 9. She said that she can brush off trolling aimed at herself but will not stay quiet when her family is dragged into the controversy.Why Rashmika Mandanna ignores social media trollsIn a recent chat with Prema – The Journalist, Rashmika Mandanna spoke about how her way of handling online hate has changed over the years. She said she once replied to people who posted unkind comments but soon understood that such exchanges led nowhere. Calling it "a waste of time", she now prefers to look away rather than get into arguments on social media.She admitted that some remarks still make her want to hit back, though experience has taught her that it is often "better to remain silent." The actress added that she is fine with people holding opinions about her acting, personality or career choices. She sees criticism as an "occupational hazard" and agrees that audiences have every right to discuss public figures.Backlash after 'Koffee with Karan' Season 9The conversation then shifted to the couple's appearance on the second episode of 'Koffee with Karan' Season 9, hosted by Karan Johar. Many viewers enjoyed their open and honest talk, yet the pair also faced heavy trolling. One moment that drew plenty of attention was Rashmika revealing that she had asked Vijay to marry her every day for a whole year.As reactions grew sharper, the couple approached the police. Their complaint covered allegedly fake posts, edited screenshots, impersonation and organised harassment across several social media platforms. Rashmika explained that she can put up with unpleasant comments about herself, but personal attacks on her loved ones cross the line.Rashmika Mandanna says she will go into warrior mode for her familyDescribing her protective side, Rashmika Mandanna brought up her upcoming action film to show how she reacts when her family is targeted. She said, "But if someone speaks about my family, I don't like it… I'll go into full warrior mode. I will go full Mysaa (her upcoming actioner). So, when you take the name of someone who is not a public figure or try to tarnish their personality, they don't deserve it, right?"The actress stressed that neither her relatives nor her friends should have to bear personal attacks just because of her profession. articles.summary: The actress, who is a longtime friend of Culkin, shares two children with her husband, Freddie Prinze Jr. —daughter Charlotte, 17, and son Rocky, 14
articles.body:
Sarah Michelle Gellar tells PEOPLE in an exclusive interview that her kids didn't realize for years that Macaulay Culkin, their "Uncle Mac," starred in Home Alone

The actress is a longtime friend of Culkin's

Gellar shares two children with her husband, Freddie Prinze Jr. —daughter Charlotte, 17, and son Rocky, 14

Sarah Michelle Gellar 's two children didn't realize for years that Home Alone 's protagonist was actually someone in their family's inner circle.

"It was so funny when my kids realized that Uncle Mac was in Home Alone ," the actress, 49, tells PEOPLE in an exclusive interview, referring to her kids — daughter Charlotte , 17, and son Rocky , 14, whom she shares with husband Freddie Prinze Jr. — and Macaulay Culkin .

"You should have seen them when they realized that. They didn't get it for so many years, and then one year they came home and they were like, 'Is Uncle Mac Kevin McCallister?" and I said, 'No,' but then, 'Yes. Your Uncle Mac is Kevin McCallister.' "

"Talk about some street cred," Gellar continues with a laugh, adding: "I will always support Uncle Mac."

Culkin, 46, starred in 1990's Home Alone and 1992's Home Alone 2: Lost in New York, holiday comedy films that follow a young child who, while left on his own during the Christmas season, creates elaborate booby traps and schemes to outsmart criminals.

The actor is reportedly set to return for a new Home Alone project, which is currently in early development at Disney.

In 2012, another film, Home Alone: The Holiday Heist , was released, and more recently, Home Sweet Home Alone premiered on Disney+ in 2021.

Gellar — who is helping Ancestry kick off its holiday campaign, Gathering the Good — and Culkin are longtime friends. They rose to fame as child actors in the 1990s and were later classmates at New York's Professional Children's School.

Prinze Jr., 50, previously told PEOPLE that he and the American Horror Story actor often play the video game BattleTech together. "He's a very good s--- talker," Prinze Jr. said of Culkin.

Culkin and his fiancée, Brenda Song , are parents to two sons : Dakota, born in 2021, and Carson, born in 2022. Last year, during his A Nostalgic Night with Macaulay Culkin tour, the actor said that despite watching Home Alone with his kids "often," they have yet to make the connection that Kevin is Culkin at age 10.

He further explained that he hopes "to keep up that illusion as long as possible."

articles.title: 40 Arunachal villages along China border see residents return: Amit Shah
articles.summary: Amit Shah says 40 Arunachal border villages saw residents return under Vibrant Villages Programme; launches Rs 5,610 crore projects and flags off medical vans.
articles.body: GUWAHATI: Improved infrastructure and modern amenities under the Centre’s Vibrant Villages Programme have encouraged residents of 40 villages, along the India-China border, to return to their native homes in Arunachal Pradesh, Union home minister Amit Shah said on Sunday.Launching development initiatives worth more than Rs 5,610 crore in the state, Shah, while addressing a cooperative festival at the Dorjee Khandu State Convention Centre in Itanagar, said the Centre was committed to transforming the northeast border villages. The event was organised under PM Modi’s “Sahkar Se Samriddhi” vision.“Earlier, people were migrating from 40 such villages in Arunachal Pradesh, but now residents have started returning and the population has increased there. Facilities relating to electricity, education, healthcare, employment and drinking water have been strengthened in these villages at the govt initiative,” Shah said.The Union home minister also unveiled the Arunachal Pradesh Cooperative Vision, 2047, and said the Vibrant Villages Programme was producing visible results along the India-China border.He said the Centre had directed ITBP and the Army to procure essential supplies from local villages and cooperative institutions to strengthen border economies, adding that the initiative had strengthened rural economies and deepened ties between border communities and security forces.Highlighting the Centre’s financial support, Shah said Arunachal Pradesh received Rs 33,530 crore between 2004 and 2014 under the UPA govt, compared to Rs 1,49,664 crore between 2014 and 2024 under the Modi govt. He said devolution funds had increased 18 times, while grants-in-aid had risen one-and-a-half times.Among major projects, he cited the 1,500-km Frontier Highway, approved at a cost of Rs 44,000 crore, and the 2,880-MW Dibang Hydropower Project, initiated at an estimated cost of Rs 32,000 crore.Shah called for expansion of cooperative-based fisheries and dairy activities to generate rural employment. He assured dairy farmers that Amul and the National Dairy Development Board would procure milk produced in the state, while efforts would be made to establish local processing facilities.He said the Modi govt had given unprecedented priority to northeast connectivity over the past 12 years, linking all state capitals in the region by rail and air.At the festival, Shah flagged off solar-powered mobile medical vans for villages in 11 border districts under the Vibrant Villages Programme and inaugurated the SARAS Mela. Equipped with telemedicine, AI-based tuberculosis screening, digital X-ray, ECG and laboratory facilities, the vans will provide healthcare services in remote areas. The mela showcased local products and traditional crafts and provided market access to women’s self-help groups.Shah later inaugurated the campus of the 12th Battalion of the National Disaster Response Force in Itanagar. “Arunachal Pradesh and the entire northeast are among the regions most vulnerable to natural disasters. All the buildings in this campus have been constructed in accordance with earthquake-resistant standards. The first line of defence against natural disasters begins with the facilities of our 12th Battalion,” Shah said.He added that the campus would serve as a disaster response centre for the northeast and neighbouring regions and train the State Disaster Response Forces of all the eight states in the region.Lauding the state’s picturesque landscape, Shah described it as the land where the Sun God first enters India and highlighted its tradition of Sun worship and association with Lord Parshuram. articles.title: Leroy Boseman, father of late 'Black Panther' star Chadwick Boseman, passes away on November 19; family asks for 'privacy, compassion and understanding'
articles.summary: Leroy Boseman, father of the late actor Chadwick Boseman, has passed away at the age of 82.
articles.body: Leroy Boseman, father of the late actor Chadwick Boseman, has passed away at the age of 82. His death comes just days before what would have been his son's 50th birthday, amid a legal dispute within the family over the 'Black Panther' star's estate.Leroy Boseman dies after a brief illnessLeroy Boseman died on Thursday, November 19, as per an obituary. The family's representative, Camille Davis, told Fox Carolina News and Complex that he had been unwell for a short time, describing it as a "brief illness".In a statement shared, the family said, "To the world, he may be known as the father of Derrick, Kevin and Chadwick Boseman. To us, he was so much more. He was a beloved husband, a father and a constant presence in our family's story. As we mourn his passing, we reflect with gratitude on the life he lived, the memories we shared and the legacy he leaves behind. During this difficult time, we remain united as a family, supporting one another and honouring his memory."They added, "We respectfully ask for privacy, compassion and understanding as our family navigates this tremendous loss."Who was Leroy Boseman?The obituary states that Leroy Boseman hailed from Belton, South Carolina. As per the report, he ran an upholstery business and also worked at a textile factory. He and his wife Carolyn raised three sons: Chadwick, Derrick and Kevin.Chadwick Boseman passed away on August 28, 2020, aged 43, after privately fighting colon cancer for four years. Speaking about him in a 2025 interview, Leroy had said, "He was a wonderful child. Everything he did was good. I can't blame him for nothing that he did for us as a family."Estate dispute with Chadwick's widowLeroy Boseman's demise follows a petition filed in Los Angeles in July by Derrick and Kevin, which named him as a party. It seeks to remove Chadwick's widow, Simone Ledward Boseman, as administrator of the late actor's estate. The brothers claim she has not distributed the remaining assets properly.As per the petition, Simone is entitled to 50 per cent of the estate because Chadwick died without a will, around six days after their 2020 wedding. His parents are entitled to 25 per cent.In a July 23 statement, Derrick and Kevin said, "For years, our parents have sought clarity regarding matters connected to the estate of our brother, Chadwick Boseman, including his intellectual property and legacy. This action was filed on behalf of, and with the authority of, our parents, Leroy and Carolyn Boseman, who assigned their respective interests in the estate to Boseman Family LLC."Tribute plans for Chadwick Boseman's birthday put on holdThe report added that the family has paused plans to honour Chadwick on what would have been his 50th birthday on Sunday, November 29, as funeral arrangements are underway.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'I Dream of Jeannie' star Barbara Eden, 95, still rides exercise bike for 35 minutes to stay fit
articles.summary: Barbara Eden reveals the stationary bike routine and personal trainer workouts keeping her fit as the "I Dream of Jeannie" star turns 95.
articles.body: Barbara Eden isn’t slowing down at all — she's actually speeding up. Despite turning 95 in August, the "I Dream of Jeannie" icon stays fit by working out on her stationary bicycle. "I go for about, I don't know, 35 minutes on the bike," Eden told Fox News Digital recently of her fitness routine. "It's good." BARBARA EDEN, 95, SAYS SHE’S ‘OKAY’ AFTER LAST-MINUTE CANCELATION OF FESTIVAL APPEARANCE The former sitcom star said that both she and her husband of 35 years, Jon Eicholtz, both have a personal trainer who comes to their home. "I don't go to the gym anymore," she revealed, adding that when she did, it was "spinning class for an hour, and then I worked with a trainer for a half hour, lifting weights." DONNA MILLS DOES 100 SIT-UPS A DAY, PLAYS TENNIS FIVE TIMES A WEEK AT 85 BUT WON'T QUIT DORITOS Eden said she still lifts weights a little. "Not as heavy as I used to." She added that weightlifting is especially good for women and their bones. "You have to be disciplined about being active when you’re an actor," she laughed when asked. "My husband and I both have a trainer that comes in and helps us out." 4 SIMPLE HABITS CAN HELP SLOW MUSCLE LOSS AS YOU AGE, FITNESS EXPERT SAYS Eden said she wasn’t sure what to credit for her longevity and energy, "but I'm glad I'm here, and I'm glad I'm still working." "I'm careful about what I eat, but I'm not overly stupid about it, you know?" she said when asked about her diet and philosophy on health. "I've never smoked. I don't know if that means anything. But, I think one of the things that's most important in your life is that you recognize other people. You realize that they're not so different than you are and that you have to get along. And when you do that, you find life is much more interesting, and people are much more interesting." The actress also has a simple beauty routine which she said is what she’s always done. It involves washing her face at night and putting on moisturizer. "That's about it," she revealed. One thing the timeless beauty said she wished she had known about when she was younger was "the damage the sun could do to your skin. We didn't know that when I was growing up. And I think it really helps, if you know, to put sunscreen, you know, on your face during the day. Or if you're working." The actress’ career spans more than 70 years, but she is best known for her titular role in the iconic sitcom "I Dream of Jeannie," which she said she never expected to become a phenomenon. ‘I DREAM OF JEANNIE’ STAR BARBARA EDEN TURNS HEADS AT 94 IN NEW PHOTO WITH HUSBAND "It makes me so happy, really so happy that people still enjoy her," Eden said. "I really never expected the show to have the longevity it has." The "Voyage to the Bottom of the Sea" star said that she gets fan mail from all over the world, including China and Russia. ‘CHARLIE’S ANGELS’ STAR JACLYN SMITH LIVED APART FROM HER HUSBAND FOR 17 YEARS DURING THEIR 35-YEAR LOVE STORY "I'm just flabbergasted when I get the mail, and very, very proud. articles.title: Jennifer Lopez claims not being a ‘typical’ White actress made it harder to land Hollywood movie roles
articles.summary: Jennifer Lopez claims Hollywood overlooked her as a Latina actress, saying she had to create her "own lane" as critics push back on social media.
articles.body: Jennifer Lopez is receiving criticism after claiming that she has struggled to land acting roles in Hollywood because she is not White, describing how she has been forced to create her "own lane" as a Latina entertainer, in an interview published on Friday. Lopez made the remarks in an interview with The New York Times, pushing back on the notion that she gets thousands of acting offers, claiming instead that Hollywood has often overlooked her because of her ethnicity. "Even from the beginning of my career, I got offered things, but I was only offered a few things. I had to kind of create things for myself," the actress said. "And the reason, I think, is because I just wasn't the typical kind of, like, to be honest, a White actress. You know what I mean? And it's still kind of the same today." 'BLUE BLOODS' STAR JENNIFER ESPOSITO SAYS SHE WALKED AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD AFTER YEARS OF REJECTION AND ‘ABUSE’ Lopez’s more recent film credits include "Office Romance" (2026), "Shotgun Wedding" (2022), "Hustlers" (2019) and "Second Act" (2018). She also secured several leading roles in the late 1990s and early 2000s, including "The Wedding Planner," "Out of Sight" and "Maid in Manhattan," and was cast as the late singer Selena Quintanilla-Perez in "Selena." JENNIFER LOPEZ ADMITS SHE 'WOULD'VE HAD SEX' WITH ENTIRE STAR-STUDDED 90S MOVIE CAST The Puerto Rican actress said Hollywood continues to look for "certain" things when casting performers, suggesting that the industry's preferences have historically made it more difficult for actors of color to secure roles. Lopez acknowledged, however, that the screen industry has made progress in improving diversity and representation. "There's a certain thing that they look for, and it's more diverse now for sure, and that's good," the actress said. "But because of that, you have to kind of create your own lane in a lot of ways," she added. "If I want to do something, I don't wait for somebody to offer me…I try to do it, and then if something comes along, great." IDRIS ELBA REJECTS 'WOKE' JAMES BOND CASTING PUSH, WARNS AUDIENCES 'WON'T GO FOR A BLACK MALE' IN THE ROLE Fox News co-host Tomi Lahren pushed back on Lopez’s claims, writing on X: "LOL, sure Jan." Internet personality Oli London noted Lopez’ robust net worth and catalog of big-screen appearances, writing on X: "JLO has appeared in 44 films and is worth $400 million." You were a bad actress, but very hot...that's why you got casted," Curry-Rhode wrote in a post to X. Movie critic Christian Toto told Fox News Digital, "Lopez has worked steadily over the past two decades, bouncing from major film projects to concerts and her solo music career. She's undeniably talented and has earned every gig that came her way. Still, for her to suggest she's been penalized by Hollywood for the color of her skin is absurd. articles.body:
“You Can See Everything,” Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes , reached an impressive box office milestone this weekend, becoming one of the few documentaries to make more than $100 million worldwide.

Variety reports that almost all of the film’s $102.4 million box office has come from U.S. audiences, from whom it has grossed $93.4 million so far.

“You Can See Everything” will be opening in many more countries over the next few months — starting with Mexico, Brazil and Argentina on Nov. 25 and 26 — so its box office total could end up significantly higher.

And while the documentary was already an undeniable commercial success for indie studio A24 (especially with a reported budget of $7 million), it could now surpass the records set by the highest grossing documentaries of all time — “March of the Penguins” ($127 million globally) and “Fahrenheit 9/11” ($222 million globally).

articles.title: Miley Cyrus and new husband Maxx Morando reveal intimate matching tattoos after Palm Springs wedding
articles.summary: The couple got married Saturday in Palm Springs, California.
articles.body:
Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando got matching ink to celebrate their new husband and wife status.

Tattoo artist Jamie Gene Lopez shared pics of the newlyweds' new nameplate tattoos on Instagram Sunday. Cyrus got "Maxx" tattooed in small capital letters on her right hip, while Morando got "Miley" on his left hip in the same style.

The two posed side by side with their arms around one another, both unbuttoning their jeans to show off their new tattoos.

Cyrus, 33, and Morando, 28, got married Saturday in an intimate wedding in Palm Springs, California. The "Flowers" singer's parents, Billy Ray Cyrus and Tish Cyrus, both attended the wedding , with their respective partners.

The "Achy Breaky Heart" singer took his fiancée, Elizabeth Hurley, as his date, while Tish was with husband Dominic Purcell.

Miley's sister Noah was also at the wedding, as was Hurley's son, Damian.

It's clear Miley is in a better place with her father these days, following years of estrangement after his 2022 divorce from Tish. The exes were married for 28 years, and share five children together — Miley, Noah, 28, Braison, 32, Brandi, 39, and Trace, 37.

Miley cried tears of joy while exchanging vows with Morando Saturday in pics obtained by Page Six. The Grammy winner smiled as she got emotional at the altar, looking gorgeous in a long-sleeved white wedding dress with white flowers in her hair.

The "Party in the U.S.A." singer and the Liily drummer have been dating since 2021, after they went on a blind date . They got engaged in December 2025 after four years of dating.

"And I'm telling you, I was so, so surprised," Miley said that month on "Good Morning America" when asked about Morando popping the question during a trip to Asia together.

"I am not easy to surprise because I love to control every situation, and I had completely surrendered," she explained.

Back in November 2024, she talked about their six-year age gap , noting in an interview with Harper's Bazaar that she was a true millennial while he was definitely Gen Z.

Still, she said they had plenty in common, including that they "don't take life too seriously."

She also said that they enjoy listening to songs they think are "cringe" but they "love," such as Train's 2001 hit "Drops of Jupiter."

articles.title: Torcedora faz marido esmeraldino torcer para o Vila Nova | G1
articles.standfirst: Luiz Augusto Proença, de 26 anos, conta que começou a acompanhar o Colorado ao lado da esposa e se identifica como torcedor do clube desde 2023. Vídeo publicado por Anna Karolina mostra a mudança de torcida da família.
articles.summary: Luiz Augusto Proença, de 26 anos, conta que começou a acompanhar o Colorado ao lado da esposa e se identifica como torcedor do clube desde 2023.
articles.body:
Uma torcedora do Vila Nova conseguiu transformar o marido, que antes torcia para o Goiás, em colorado. A mudança de Luiz Augusto Proença, de 26 anos, foi registrada pela esposa, Anna Tereza, em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais. Na publicação, ela brincou com a nova torcida do companheiro “A mulher sábia edifica a sua casa”.

A história, no entanto, não aconteceu de uma hora para outra. Luiz conta que aprendeu a torcer pelo Goiás ainda criança, por influência do pai, com quem frequentava o estádio. Apesar disso, ele diz que não acompanhava tão de perto os resultados do clube e tinha mais interesse pelo futebol europeu.

A aproximação com o Vila Nova começou durante o namoro. Em 2016, ele foi pela primeira vez ao estádio para acompanhar um jogo do Colorado com Anna. Na época, o time disputava o acesso da Série C para a Série B.

“Eu só fui para acompanhar ela mesmo. Só que o que eu achei legal na torcida do Vila é que é uma torcida muito apaixonada”, contou.

Segundo Luiz, a energia dos torcedores foi um dos fatores que fizeram com que ele se identificasse com o clube.

Ele passou a frequentar os jogos com a esposa e, com o passar dos anos, a acompanhar mais de perto a rotina do time. “Eu me identifico como torcedor do Vila Nova desde 2023”, afirmou.

Ele explica que, no começo, ia ao estádio ocasionalmente. Atualmente, acompanha praticamente todos os jogos e também se tornou sócio-torcedor do clube.

Antes e depois de torcedor do Goiás virar Vila Nova — Foto: Reprodução/ Instagram Anna Tereza

A paixão pelo Vila Nova também passou a fazer parte da rotina familiar. Quando o filho do casal, João Gabriel, ainda era pequeno, Anna começou a levá-lo ao estádio. Hoje, aos 3 anos, ele já acompanha os jogos e canta músicas da torcida.

Luiz diz que acompanhar o filho e a esposa nas arquibancadas também fortaleceu sua identificação com o Colorado.

“Poder vivenciar isso com o meu filho, uma coisa que eu tive com o meu pai, de ter meu pai presente e poder estar presente na vida do meu filho no estádio, cara, é muito legal”, disse.

O corretor imobiliário conta que a mudança foi uma construção ao longo dos anos, influenciada pela convivência com a família e pela identificação com a história e a torcida do Vila Nova.

Casal com filho torcendo para o Vila Nova — Foto: Reprodução/ Instagram Anna Tereza

Não liga para críticas e mantém carinho pelo pai

Luiz conta que aprendeu a torcer pelo Goiás ainda criança, por influência do pai, que o levava ao estádio e lhe dava camisas do clube. Apesar de ter crescido acompanhando o time, ele diz que nunca teve uma paixão tão grande pelo Esmeraldino. Na época, gostava principalmente de estar ao lado do pai e da família nos jogos, mas não costumava acompanhar os resultados ou a situação do clube.

A mudança de torcida também rendeu brincadeiras dentro de casa. O pai, que foi responsável por apresentá-lo ao futebol e ao Goiás, encarou a decisão com bom humor.

“Meu pai falou assim: ‘Bom que você já aprende a sofrer, que a vida é sofrida, né? Então vai lá sofrer pro Vila’”, contou Luiz, ao lembrar da reação.

Apesar da mudança de lado no futebol, ele mantém a admiração pelo pai e destaca a importância da relação dos dois.

Luiz também diz que não se incomoda com as críticas de outros torcedores pela troca de camisa. Para ele, é melhor assumir a identificação que construiu com o Vila Nova do que continuar dizendo que torce por um clube com o qual não se sente mais conectado.

“Eu sou melhor torcendo para o Vila e sendo verdadeiro com aquilo que sinto do que ficar torcendo para o Goiás frustrado, querendo torcer para outro clube”, afirmou

articles.body: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi's 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' continued its impressive box-office run on Sunday, November 22. Its domestic net total is now nearing the Rs 1,000 cr milestone, while its worldwide gross has crossed Rs 1,690 cr.Ramayana Movie ReviewThe film collected Rs 35.60 cr in India net collections on Day 18 through 16,277 shows. The Hindi version led with Rs 26.25 cr from 13,852 shows. Malayalam contributed Rs 3.40 cr, while Kannada added Rs 2.50 cr. Tamil and Telugu earned Rs 2.40 cr and Rs 1.05 cr, respectively.With these collections, the film's India gross has reached Rs 1,126.50 cr, against a net total of Rs 942.75 cr. Its overseas gross stands at Rs 567 cr, taking the worldwide gross to Rs 1,693.50 cr.'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' records a Sunday jump in collectionsAccording to Sacnilk, 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' earned 28.8% more on Day 18 than the Rs 27.65 cr collected on Day 17. However, the latest Sunday total was 52.5% lower than the Rs 75 cr recorded on the corresponding Sunday a week earlier.The film's average collection per show stood at Rs 21,881. Its three-day weekend total, covering Days 16 to 18, reached Rs 79 cr in India net collections. The first eight days had contributed Rs 564.60 cr net and Rs 675.05 cr gross. During the next seven days, the film earned Rs 299.15 cr net and Rs 357.10 cr gross, marking a 47% decline.The third weekend added Rs 79 cr net and Rs 94.35 cr gross. articles.summary: HBO has unveiled the first full scene from its upcoming 'Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone' series, giving fans a glimpse of the new adaptation.
articles.body: HBO has unveiled the first full scene from its upcoming 'Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone' series, giving fans a glimpse of the new adaptation. One of the standout moments is the notable changes from JK Rowling book.The approximately 90-second clip features Harry Potter arriving in the Great Hall alongside Ron Weasley as Albus Dumbledore prepares to begin the feast. While the setting is familiar to fans of the franchise, the scene introduces a few differences from the original story. As reported by Collider, one of the noticeable changes involves students chanting Dumbledore's name, an addition that does not feature in Rowling's novel.Hogwarts moment gets a new interpretationAnother departure comes when Harry asks Ron whether Dumbledore is a little mad. In the book, Harry directs the same question to Ron's older brother, Percy Weasley. However, the biggest change comes in an exchange between Dumbledore and Professor Minerva McGonagall. The two share a private conversation about Harry, with McGonagall commenting on his resemblance to his father, James Potter. The interaction is not part of the original novel, which narrates the banquet sequence from Harry's perspective.The addition has given way to speculation that the HBO series could go beyond the book pages and explore new perspectives.The Great Hall feast is among the most memorable moments brought to life by director Chris Columbus in 2001's 'Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone' film adaptation.'Harry Potter' series runtimeFans can expect to see a lot more new inclusions into the series as episode runtimes have reportedly leaked ahead of the December 25 premiere. As per the leaks, the runtime for the eight-part series is as follows:Episode 1 – 1 hour and 6 minutesEpisode 2 – 51 minutesEpisode 3 – 54 minutesEpisode 4 – 48 minutesEpisode 5 – 56 minutesEpisode 6 – 52 minutesEpisode 7 – 59 minutesEpisode 8 – 1 hour and 9 minutesThe full season thus has a total runtime of over 7.5 hours, thus giving the series roughly 5 hours more runtime than the first movie adaptation.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: John Malkovich opens up to "60 Minutes" about losing his entire fortune to Bernie Madoff's Ponzi scheme and the moment he told his wife the news.
articles.body: John Malkovich recalled once losing his entire fortune to disgraced financier Bernie Madoff. Malkovich, 72, told "60 Minutes" that he had recently returned from directing a play in Mexico City when he found out about Madoff's Ponzi scheme. "I got home from that and I saw this photograph of Bernie Madoff in handcuffs, and I thought, 'Oh, well that could prove interesting,'" Malkovich said. "I went in and said to my wife, you know, 'I'm just going to go around the corner, buy a pack of cigarettes.'" FRAUD MASTERMIND BEHIND MULTIMILLION-DOLLAR PONZI SCHEME THAT VICTIMIZED TRAVIS KELCE IS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT He added, "I said, 'We have a little problem. Bernie Madoff just got arrested.'" Malkovich, a previous smoker, hadn't indulged in nicotine "for a while" when he left the house that day, he said. "That was pretty much everything I'd ever made," he admitted before coming to terms with his situation. "You know, you look to blame, you're going to do this and that, and then you realize, 'Look, why don't you shut up?'" No matter what they do. Get on with your life and that's it." Madoff died in April 2021 while serving a 150-year sentence at the federal medical care center in Butner, North Carolina, where his attorney said he was being treated for terminal kidney failure. A decades-long force on Wall Street, Madoff shocked the world when he pleaded guilty in 2009 to running a vast Ponzi scheme that prosecutors said swindled thousands out of their life savings. The scheme began in the early 1970s, and by the time Madoff was arrested in December 2008, had defrauded as many as 37,000 people in 136 countries out of up to $65 billion. Prosecutors contend he started defrauding investors much earlier. articles.title: Don Toliver Concert Evacuated After ‘Substance Believed to Be Tear Gas’ Was Released into Arena Crowd
articles.summary: The rapper is next scheduled to perform in London on Monday, Nov. 23
articles.body:
Don Toliver's arena concert at Co-op Live in Manchester, England, was evacuated during his performance on Nov. 22

Greater Manchester Police said, "It is understood that a substance believed to be tear gas was let off in the crowd towards the end of a concert"

The rapper, who was nominated for five awards at the 2027 Grammys, is next scheduled to perform in London on Monday, Nov. 23

Don Toliver 's concert was evacuated during the tail end of his performance.

During the arena concert at Co-op Live in Manchester, England, on Sunday, Nov. 22, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) described the situation in a news release as "a major incident," just six days after the rapper, 32, was nominated five times at the 2027 Grammy Awards .

"Officers alongside other emergency services personnel are currently in attendance following an incident at Co-op Live this evening," the police statement read. "It is understood that a substance believed to be tear gas was let off in the crowd towards the end of a concert."

The release from authorities continued, "All attendees are currently being safely evacuated as a precaution. Those showing signs of being impacted are being supported by emergency services, with no serious injuries reported."

Police cautioned everyone to go home and stay away from the venue.

"Please stay away from the arena whilst emergency services help those that have been at the concert safely make their way to their transport home," authorities said.

"A major incident has been declared to ensure emergency services and partner agencies can work together quickly and effectively to coordinate a safe response," they added.

Toliver's last Instagram Stories posts before the concert incident, part of his Octane World Tour, showed him traveling to Manchester while playing what appeared to be Grand Theft Auto VI on a private plane.

His next concert, the final stop on the tour, is scheduled for the O2 Arena in London on Monday, Nov. 23.

articles.title: Shrewsbury musician Danny Griffiths joins Two Door Cinema Club's tour
articles.summary: Danny Griffiths spent years playing pub gigs to tiny crowds before a social media video changed everything.
articles.body:
A little over a year ago, Danny Griffiths was delivering supermarket shopping and posting videos online that barely anyone watched.

In February, he will be touring Europe with internationally successful indie band Two Door Cinema Club.

The speed of the change still catches him by surprise.

"I posted one video online and woke up the next morning and it had just gone mental," he said.

"I phoned my dad and said: 'No way, it's going, it's going'."

That moment became a turning point for the young musician, who had spent countless evenings playing pub gigs, writing songs and sharing videos online in the hope that someone might be listening.

Videos of Griffiths performing his own songs regularly show packed crowds singing along to his songs, while his track, Lightweight Champion, has attracted more than half a million streams on Spotify.

"The next gig, everyone knew that one bit of the song. It was such a surreal feeling."

The attention may look like the result of an overnight success, but the reality was countless hours of persistence.

Before the streaming figures and growing fanbase, Griffiths was balancing music with shifts as a supermarket delivery driver, fitting gigs and songwriting around work whenever he could.

"There have been so many pub gigs that I've done where no-one's been there," he said.

"There were so many things that went wrong."

Yet he kept writing, performing and posting videos online several times a week.

Most attracted little attention, before one clip suddenly "went nuts", introducing his music to an audience far beyond the pubs where he had been honing his craft.

Music itself had arrived almost by chance. During the Covid pandemic, Griffiths picked up an old guitar that belonged to his sister and began teaching himself to play.

The first song he learned was Leaving on a Jet Plane.

"I remember it being so annoying for my dad because it was the only song I could play for about two weeks straight," he laughed.

As his confidence grew, he moved from cover versions to writing songs of his own, gradually discovering that audiences responded most strongly to material that came from his own experiences.

That journey began in Shrewsbury, where Griffiths attended Crowmoor Primary School, Belvidere School and later studied at Welsh Bridge campus. He started performing in pubs around the town and still returns regularly to play homecoming gigs at the Bricklayers Arms.

Those shows have become something of a measure of how far he has come.

"When I come home we'll put on a gig there and there'll be hundreds turning up," he said.

"There were people that had come from Ipswich and Sheffield. People flew over from Ireland to come to the Bricklayers gig.

Griffiths has also shared stages with artists including The Kooks, Razorlight, James, Jamie Webster and The Cheap Thrills, taking him from local pub stages to some of the country's biggest live music audiences.

Next year's European tour with Two Door Cinema Club is the biggest opportunity of his career so far. It will also include his first headline show in Germany.

Yet even with a European tour in the diary and crowds singing along to his songs, Griffiths still finds himself stopping occasionally to reflect on how much life has changed since the days of delivering shopping and playing to near-empty rooms.

"Today's one of the only times in a few months where I've stopped and thought, 'What is actually going on?'" he said.

articles.title: A resurgent ‘Hunger Games’ goes big at the box office, despite competition of ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’
articles.summary: Fourteen years and six movies in, “The Hunger Games” franchise rediscovered its box-office might, as “Sunrise on the Reaping” debuted with $120 million in North American theaters over the weekend.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Fourteen years and six movies in, “The Hunger Games” franchise rediscovered its box-office might, as “Sunrise on the Reaping” debuted with $120 million in North American theaters over the weekend, according to studio estimates Sunday. The sun had seemed to be setting on “The Hunger Games” as a cultural force. After the original blockbuster run of four movies led by Jennifer Lawrence, Lionsgate’s 2023 prequel, “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes,” topped off at $361.8 million worldwide — a decent sum but about half what each of the first four movies grossed. Yet “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” has restored the Suzanne Collins adaptations to blockbuster status. The film, a sequel to “Songbirds and Snakes” and set 25 years before the original series, launched with $225 million worldwide on its opening weekend. Lionsgate produced and distributed the movie, budgeted at about $150 million. “It’s obviously not common for a film in its sixth installment to completely reverse the trajectory, but it’s awfully satisfying to be a part of it,” said Adam Fogelson, chairman of the Lionsgate Motion Picture Group. At a time when movie series longevity is far from assured, “Sunrise on the Reaping” managed to notch the year’s fifth $100 million-plus domestic launch — something only accomplished in 2026 by some of the most bankable franchises: Spider-Man (“Spider-Man: Brand New Day”), Toy Story (“Toy Story 5”), Super Mario (“The Super Mario Galaxy Movie”) and whatever Christopher Nolan makes (“The Odyssey”). And it did it while a significant portion of potential moviegoers were locked at home playing “Grand Theft Auto VI.” How ‘Hunger Games’ pulled off a box-office comeback Yet Gen Z again powered a big weekend in theaters. Some 74% of the audience for the “Hunger Games” prequel-sequel were aged 18-34. Several of 2026’s box-office hits — including “Obsession,” “Backrooms” and “You Can See Everything” — have likewise succeeded by packing theaters with the most potent demographic in moviegoing. While “Sunrise on the Reaping” includes a supporting cast of well-known veteran stars (Ralph Fiennes, Kieran Culkin, Elle Fanning, Jesse Plemons), the movie largely belongs to a new generation of young actors: Jo Zada, Mckenna Grace, Ben Wang and Whitney Peak. The film, directed by Francis Lawrence, is centered around teenage Haymitch Abernathy (Zada), the role originally played by Woody Harrelson. Fogelson credits several things to the “Hunger Games” turnaround. “Songbirds and Snakes” was an origin story of a villain, and thus a darker tale. “Sunrise on the Reaping” has the Hunger Games themselves more front and center. It focuses on the backstory of a beloved character in Haymitch. And the cast, a mix of newcomers and veterans, elevated the film. “It’s consistent with how ‘The Hunger Games’ has always operated. Jennifer Lawrence wasn’t the mega movie star when this franchise started with her,” Fogelson says. “There is no question that part of the incredible resurgence we’ve seen at the box office has been Gen Z and Gen Alpha demonstrating how much they love going to movie theaters.” Reviews were ok (67% fresh on Rotten Tomatoes), but audience scores were better. “Sunrise on the Reaping” earned an “A-” CinemaScore from moviegoers, a tick up from the “B+” received by “Songbirds and Snakes.” ‘I Play Rocky’ scores a rare ‘A+’ CinemaScore In its first weekend of wide release, Amazon MGM Studios’ “I Play Rocky” came in second with $9.3 million from 2,477 locations. Peter Farrelly’s comic drama about the making of “Rocky” stars Anthony Ippolito as a young Sylvester Stallone. It has previously played in limited release for two weeks. The biggest win for “I Play Rocky” — a potential Oscar contender — wasn’t its bottom-line gross, but its CinemaScore: an A+. Such a high mark is rare. (Even “The Odyssey” didn’t score so well.) But Farrelly has managed it before. His best picture-winning 2018 film “Green Book” got the same score. Ticket sales were down about 10% from the same weekend last year, when “Wicked For Good” came out, according to data firm Rentrak. But they were up 84.9% from last weekend. From the earliest stage of dating “Sunrise on the Reaping,” Lionsgate analyzed the benefits and risks of going up against “Grand Theft Auto.” Ultimately, the studio believed both could coexist. Some 67% of the audience for the “Hunger Games” film was female. “Many have speculated as to whether the release of ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ would hurt ‘The Hunger Games’ at the box office this weekend, and I think the marketplace has already spoken,” said Paul Dergarabedian, head of marketplace trends for Rentrak. “Both can do just fine.” Last week’s No. 1 film, “Ebenezer,” starring Johnny Depp, dipped 60% in its second weekend with $7.7 million. The Paramount release has grossed $32.5 million domestically and $45.9 million internationally. Hollywood will now turn its attention to a Thanksgiving holiday weekend full of intrigue. “Sunrise on the Reaping” will be competing with a variety of new releases: Universal’s “Focker in Law,” the Disney animated film “Hexed,” Netflix’s IMAX release of “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” and Neon’s wide release of James Gray’s crime drama “Paper Tiger.” Top 10 movies by domestic box office With final domestic figures being released Monday, this list factors in the estimated ticket sales for Friday through Sunday at U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to Rentrak: 1. “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” $120 million. 2. “I Play Rocky,” $9.3 million. 3. “Ebenezer,” $7.7 million. 4. “The Cat in the Hat,” $6.9 million. 5. “Godzilla Minus Zero,” $2.7 million. 6. “You Can See Everything,” $2.5 million. 7. “Wild Horse Nine,” $2.5 million. 8. “Ghost Soldier,” $2.4 million. 9. “Wildwood,” $2.3 million. 10. “Ramayana,” $2.1 million.
