articles.summary: Singer Miley Cyrus married rock drummer Maxx Morando in an intimate weekend wedding in Palm Springs, California, according to a post on her Instagram account.
articles.body: Singer Miley Cyrus married rock drummer Maxx Morando in an intimate weekend wedding in Palm Springs, California, according to a post on her Instagram account. The post said Cyrus, 33, and Morando, 28, were wed on Saturday. Photographs show the couple embracing in front of a white backdrop with a palm tree characteristic of the Palm Springs desert in the background, a large dog lying at their feet. In one photo, the couple kisses standing in an aisle of white roses. The “Party in the U.S.A.” singer wore a long-sleeve silk Saint Laurent gown by Anthony Vaccarello and elegant white silk kitten heels, according to a statement from Saint Laurent. The dress had a low back, and she wore flowers in her hair, which was pulled back into an updo. Morando wore dark, square shades. His single-breasted tuxedo was also made by the French luxury fashion brand. The pair have been together since 2021, meeting after they were set up on a blind date, according to an interview Cyrus gave to Vogue in 2023. Morando proposed to her while the couple were in Japan late last year, he said in a separate interview with Wonderland Magazine. “I could feel my heart pounding” before popping the question, Morando said for a profile in the magazine. Morando is the drummer of the rock band Liily.

articles.title: Bustamante y su fortuna tras salir de 'Operación Triunfo': "Ganaba más dinero en una noche que en un año"
articles.standfirst: El cantante reflexiona sobre su paso por la academia de 'OT'
articles.summary: El cantante reflexiona sobre su paso por la academia de 'OT'
articles.body: La vida de David Bustamante cambió cuando entró en la academia de 'Operación Triunfo'. Como el resto de sus compañeros del concurso, el ahora cantante pasó de tener un trabajo normal y corriente a disfrutar de ingresos que jamás había alcanzado. "Ganaba más dinero en una noche que en un año", ha señalado el cántabro en el pódcast 'Poco se habla', de Xuso Jones y Ana Brito. El impacto en su vida personal, y económica, fue enorme. La repercusión del programa convirtió a desconocidos en famosos casi al instante. El fenómeno fue muy sonado. "Yo entré siendo Titín, de San Vicente de la Barquera y a los dos meses y medio había 10.000 personas con camisetas con mi cara en mi tierra", ha comentado. "Viajábamos en un avión privado, el avión de 'Operación Triunfo'", ha recordado. Es evidente que su vida ha cambiado desde que trabajaba en la obra. Bustamante, de todas formas, ha reconocido que su verdadero éxito no es ver las cifras de su cuenta corriente: "Es ver la calidad que tiene mi familia. Cuando me cambió la vida le dije a mi padre, 'se acabó, ya no trabajas más'. Y desde entonces cuido yo de todos". Cuando dejó el programa, el artista, con una gran popularidad desde entonces hasta la actualidad, compró una casa para sus padres en su pueblo natal. Preguntado por la relación con sus excompañeros en 'Operación Triunfo', David Bustamante ha explicado que es muy positiva. "Yo me llevo bien con todos. Pero, ¿verlos? Hay gente a la que no veo en un año", ha reflexionado. De todas formas, ha defendido que cada etapa tiene su momento: "La gente no puede vivir anclada en el pasado. Es como si yo quedara todos los viernes a tomar botellines con los compañeros de la obra. No, eso ya pasó".

He later watched cultural performances at the festival.GJUST vice-chancellor Prof Vijay Kumar said the visit would expose students and faculty to global cultural and academic perspectives and strengthen avenues for research, academic collaboration and cultural exchange between Indian and Palestinian educational institutions.Sanskar Bharati regional organising secretary Vijay Kumar, registrar Dr Vijay Kumar, dean of international affairs Prof Om Prakash Sangwan and dean of student welfare Prof MK Sharma were present. articles.title: Blade Runner 2099 is an inventive twist on a cyberpunk classic
articles.summary: Blade Runner 2099 revives the classic cyberpunk world with an eight-episode series that streams on Prime Video on November 25th.
articles.body: In an age of streaming shows designed to appeal to distracted viewers, Blade Runner 2099 can feel like a welcome anachronism. The Amazon series is slow and methodical, just like the movies it follows, as it delves deep into moral ambiguity. It is very Blade Runner, in that it both feels true to the films but also expands on them in novel ways, showing you sides of this universe that have only been hinted at before. It’s just a little too long for its own good. Like the movies, 2099 uses the lens of a detective story to explore a much bigger narrative about what it means to be human. The show takes place 50 years after the last film, and a lot has changed. The Blade Runner series is set in a future where humans have developed artificial life-forms called replicants that are nearly indistinguishable from people aside from a few key traits, like being stronger and having a limited lifespan. This made them ideal for working in harsh environments, but they also became second-class citizens, many of whom were willing to fight for whatever kind of life they could, no matter how short. In between the events of 2049 and 2099 there was a war between humans and replicants, which flipped the dynamic: Now the replicants are in charge, with humans cataloged and relegated to manual labor. The titular blade runners, a kind of special detective force, are now replicants hunting down any humans who go against this new order. This sets up a curious dynamic for the show, which centers on two blade runner partners. Olwen (Michelle Yeoh) is a replicant with only a week left to live, spending her remaining time hunting down her missing ex-partner. Soon she’s joined by Cora (Hunter Schafer), a human fugitive posing as a replicant in a ploy to earn freedom for herself and her sick brother. This premise allows the show to explore the universe from a few new angles. For one thing, the ambiguity over the differences between humans and replicants becomes even cloudier with the roles reversed. Despite having longer lives and the benefit of an actual childhood (replicants are grown in a lab and enter the world as full-grown adults), people in this time are mostly emotional husks, forced to become subservient just to survive. That’s the main reason Cora is able to successfully go undercover. Her rough upbringing hardened her emotionally, making her more capable of pretending to be a replicant — a being who does not experience emotions like empathy or embarrassment. [Media: As blade running partners, the two are pulled across retrofuturistic Los Angeles with very different goals in mind, but they ultimately intersect as Olwen searches for her partner and Cora searches for freedom. I won’t spoil too much, but there’s a MacGuffin that comes into play that has existential ramifications for replicant and human alike, and both detectives are ultimately pulled into its orbit. Exploration of this premise expands the universe of Blade Runner. Some developments are largely implied — you don’t actually see the war, only its aftermath, and there are rumors of a Mexico City that remains a safe haven for humans — but others are shown in exquisite detail. There are parlors where replicants can live out different lives using disturbingly realistic bodysuits, and dingy, underground dance clubs where humans let loose away from replicant eyes. It helps that 2099 looks incredible, evoking the scuffed-up cyberpunk future of the films through chunky computers and intimidatingly brutalist architecture. And yes, both Olwen and Cora wear extremely cool jackets, like all blade runners should. The main issue is that the series feels like it stretches itself too thin at times, particularly during the middle episodes, which can sag with unnecessary storylines and characters that are underdeveloped. This is exacerbated by the slow-burn structure, which works well for a film but can feel a bit much across eight episodes. Potentially fascinating characters, like a delightfully deranged replicant played by Amy Lennox, feel disappointingly flat. 2099 tries to fill up some of its time by being more action-focused compared to the films, but these scenes often feel at odds with the rest of the show. And as much as I love tense sequences, like the Voight-Kampff test where characters stare each other down like gunslingers in a Western waiting for someone to make a wrong move, this happens a few too many times during the show, diluting the scenes’ impact. Perhaps the best thing about Blade Runner 2099 is that it ends at all. In an age when franchises are frequently bled dry, 2099 is a relatively brief and welcome dip back into a beloved universe, one with a very final finale. It’s an ending that, much like the original film, opens up all kinds of new questions — ones that may never be answered. Blade Runner 2099 starts streaming on Amazon Prime Video on November 25th.

articles.title: Diljit Dosanjh gives lifetime free ticket to fan who attended seven AURA India Tour shows at Ahmedabad concert: 'Aaj ton baad tussi meri ticket nahi khareedni hai'
articles.summary: Diljit Dosanjh melted hearts at his Ahmedabad concert on November 21 by offering free entry for life to a fan who had watched seven shows of his AURA
articles.body: Diljit Dosanjh melted hearts at his Ahmedabad concert on November 21 by offering free entry for life to a fan who had watched seven shows of his AURA India Tour 2026. The Punjabi star also spoke about the criticism around his songs and pointed to Coldplay, and clips of both moments are now going viral.Fan who attended seven shows gets a big surpriseDuring the Ahmedabad show, Diljit Dosanjh noticed a woman in the crowd who had followed his tour across several cities. He started by asking her how many concerts she had been to this year."Tuada kidva show hai is saal da? (How many shows of mine have you attended this year?)"She replied that it was seven. The singer was visibly impressed and praised her dedication."Wow… Inna da 7th show hai is saal da, Aura Tour da. Eh Vancouver vi aaye, America vi aaye, Europe vi aaye, Wembley vi aaye, ajj eh Ahmedabad vi aaye… Zordaar taadiyan innan layi! (Wow! This is their seventh show of the year on the Aura Tour. They came to Vancouver, America, Europe, Wembley, and now they've come to Ahmedabad… A big round of applause for them!)"Lifetime free pass announced on stageDiljit Dosanjh then told her she no longer needed to purchase tickets for his concerts and announced a free pass valid for life.He said, "Aaj ton baad, for your whole life, jinna chir main gaunga, tuhadi ticket free hai. Tussi sirf sanu dassna hai. Tuhadi ticket free hai. Aaj ton baad tussi meri ticket nahi khareedni hai. Aaj ton baad tuhadi ticket free hai. Jinna chir main gaunga, tuhadi ticket free hai. Thank you so much! (From today onwards, you won't have to buy tickets anymore. No, I swear, I'm serious about this. From today onwards, for your entire life, as long as I keep singing, your tickets will be free. You just have to let us know. Your tickets will be free. From today onwards, you don't have to buy tickets to my shows. As long as I keep singing, your tickets will be free. Thank you so much!)"Diljit Dosanjh questions double standards and mentions ColdplayPerforming at the Narendra Modi Stadium on Saturday, the singer also touched upon the controversy around his own songs. He wondered why his tracks faced restrictions when global acts such as Coldplay could perform songs with lyrics about being drunk and high.Diljit said, "Lekin ek baat main kahun aapse, jab Coldplay ka band gaata hai, wo gaata hai 'I'm feeling drunk and high', tab toh kisi ko dikkat nahi hoti. Agar Coldplay yahan pe aake gaate hain, 'I'm feeling drunk and high', toh kisi ko problem nahi hai. Diljit gaayega toh problem hai. Ye double standards kyun hai? (But let me tell you something. When Coldplay sings, 'I'm feeling drunk and high', nobody has a problem. When Coldplay comes here and sings those lyrics, nobody has an issue. But when Diljit sings, there's a problem. Why these double standards?)"Diljit Dosanjh's next concert is set to take place on November 27, 2026, at 4:00 PM at the Mahalaxmi Race Course in Mumbai.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Quote of the day by Matthew McConaughey: 'To succeed, we need to do good, hard work. But is it the right kind of hard work?' A powerful lesson highlighting the importance of smart work over hard work
articles.summary: Explore Matthew McConaughey's insightful message about the difference between hard work and intentional effort. Discover how to align your actions with true success in both personal and professional pursuits.
articles.body: We tend to treat hard work as the surest way to get ahead. We stuff our calendars, say yes to one more thing, then another, and keep going because surely all that effort will pay off someday, right? But what if all that hard work isn't actually taking us where we want to go?Matthew McConaughey has an interesting take on this familiar idea. The Oscar-winning actor encourages people to look past how many hours they put in and ask whether those efforts really mean something. His message isn't about dodging hard work. It's about knowing what deserves our time, energy and attention.Today's quote of the day by 'Interstellar' star Matthew McConaughey reads: “We all know that, to succeed, we need to do good, hard work. But is it the right kind of hard work?”What does Matthew McConaughey's quote mean?Matthew McConaughey shared this thought on 'The Brian Buffini Show' in January 2021, when he settled in for a warm, open conversation about his memoir 'Greenlights'.In the conversation, hosted by Brian Buffini, the actor opened up about success, happiness and figuring out what truly matters to you. They also got into how he changed the direction of his career and stepped away from the romantic comedy roles that had once defined his image.His question gets at the difference between being busy and actually making progress. You can spend a whole day ticking off tasks, meeting deadlines and taking on responsibilities, and still feel miles away from your bigger goals. Working hard matters, no doubt.The quote also reminds us what success means to us. It's easy to follow a way just because family or society expects it. McConaughey invites us to pause and ask if our choices are building the life we actually want. Sometimes the answer isn't doing more, but focusing on what truly makes a difference.Why does Matthew McConaughey's message still matter today?In a world that loves to celebrate constant productivity, taking a break or changing direction can feel like you're falling behind.. People compare their achievements with others and may measure their worth through promotions, money, recognition or the number of things they accomplish in a day.McConaughey's message offers a useful way to look at that pressure. Progress doesn't always mean saying yes to every opportunity or taking on every responsibility. Sometimes it looks like setting a boundary, learning something new, trying a different approach, or letting go of something that's stopped working for you.This applies to students, professionals and anyone chasing a personal goal. A student getting ready for an important exam might put in hours of studying without ever stopping to figure out which methods really work best for them. And someone building a career may keep piling on extra work without stopping to ask whether it supports where they want to be in the long run.The point isn't to second-guess every decision or expect instant results. It's simply to make your effort more intentional. Hard work becomes truly valuable when it's backed by clarity, patience and a willingness to adapt.Matthew McConaughey's early lifeMatthew McConaughey was born on November 4, 1969, in Uvalde, Texas. He grew up in Longview as the youngest of three sons. His mother was a teacher, while his father worked in the oil-pipe business.He initially considered studying law at the University of Texas at Austin but eventually chose film. A chance meeting with casting director Don Phillips opened the first door into the entertainment industry for him. His early experiences and the change in his academic path, laid the groundwork for a career that carried him far beyond anything he'd ever planned.How did Matthew McConaughey rise to fame?McConaughey first turned heads as the effortlessly cool David Wooderson in Richard Linklater's 'Dazed and Confused' (1993). After that, things really took off, with 'A Time to Kill' (1996), 'Contact' (1997) and 'Amistad' (1997) making him a name people knew.In the 2000s, he became a go-to name for romantic comedies, with 'The Wedding Planner' (2001), 'How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days' (2003) and 'Failure to Launch' (2006). But he didn't stay there. He later chose more varied and challenging roles in films such as 'The Lincoln Lawyer' (2011), 'Mud' (2012) and 'Magic Mike' (2012).Playing Ron Woodroof in 'Dallas Buyers Club' (2013) was the big turning point, and it won him the Academy Award for Best Actor. He also earned acclaim for the television series 'True Detective' and appeared in Christopher Nolan's 'Interstellar' (2014).Beyond acting, McConaughey also became an author with his 2020 memoir 'Greenlights,' where he looks back on his own life, the choices he made in his career and the lessons he picked up along the way. And honestly, his story gives that question about hard work real weight.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Video: How Ramos started and finished Milan’s second-goal move
articles.summary: Gonçalo Ramos scored Milan’s second goal against Frosinone in Serie A on Sunday: a video shows how the Portuguese forward sparked the Rossoneri’s attack from...
articles.body:
Gonçalo Ramos scored Milan's second goal against Frosinone in Serie A on Sunday: a video shows how the Portuguese forward sparked the Rossoneri's attack from deep in his own half before finishing at the other end of the pitch.

Milan striker Gonçalo Ramos scored his first goal in his last five Serie A matches on Sunday, adding his name to the scoresheet in a commanding 5-1 win against Frosinone at San Siro.

ITALY – NOVEMBER 22: Goncalo Ramos of AC Milan reacts after being substituted during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Frosinone Calcio at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on November 22, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

A video Milan shared on X shows Ramos making the first and final touch in the build-up to their second goal against the Ciociari.

The ex-PSG striker recovered possession near Milan's defensive box and made the run forward, while Diego Moreira and Adrien Rabiot sparked the attack on the right flank.

ITALY – NOVEMBER 22: Goncalo Ramos of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team's second goal during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Frosinone Calcio at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on November 22, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Rabiot's final pass found Ramos alone inside the box, allowing the Portuguese to score his third Serie A goal this season.

Ramos has also provided two assists in 13 league games so far.
